newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to review corporate, capital gains tax.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to review corporate, capital gains tax.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party said on Thursday it would consider changing the corporate and capital gains tax regimes if it took power.

Unveiling its campaign manifesto for elections due on May 1, Labour said: "We will review the corporate and capital gains tax regimes to see how the tax system can promote greater long-term investment."

It also said a Labour government would introduce a new individual savings account and extend the principle of tax-exempt savings schemes, known as TESSAs, and personal equity plans -- PEPs -- to promote more long-term investment.
On Wednesday, the ruling Conservatives pledged to "build on the success" that already allows 4.5 million people to benefit from TESSAs, and another 2.5 million to hold PEPs.
UK elections are set for May 1 and Labour, riding high in the opinion polls, is poised to take power for the first time since 1979.
